# Just Acoustics

> Just Acoustics is a Singapore-based acoustic treatment company that supplies and installs acoustic panels for offices, restaurants, churches, schools, studios, gyms, cinemas, and homes. Services include site assessment, custom panel design, and full installation. Established 2022.

## Typical installed prices (SGD, supply + installation)
Room sizes: small under 15 m², medium 15–40 m², large 40–100 m², very large 100 m²+. Final price is confirmed after reviewing the room; very large rooms usually need a site visit.
- Office / meeting room: small S$1,000–2,000; medium S$2,500–4,000; large S$4,000–8,000; very large from S$8,000.
- Restaurant / café: small S$1,000–2,000; medium S$2,000–4,000; large S$4,000–6,000; very large from S$6,000.
- School / classroom: small S$1,000–2,000; medium S$2,000–3,500; large S$3,500–6,500; very large from S$6,500.
- Church / hall: small from S$1,500; medium from S$4,000; large from S$6,000; very large (main sanctuaries) from S$15,000, typically S$15,000–40,000+.
- Home / living room: small S$1,000–1,800; medium S$1,500–3,000; large S$3,000–5,000; very large from S$5,000.
- Home studio: small S$1,000–2,000; medium S$2,000–3,500; large from S$3,500; very large from S$6,000.

## Key facts
- Acoustic treatment improves sound quality inside a room by absorbing and managing reflections. It does not by itself stop sound travelling through walls, floors, doors, or windows.
- Just Acoustics provides consultation, acoustic panel supply, custom design, and installation across Singapore.
- Product performance, fire requirements, final dimensions, and installation methods are confirmed for the individual product and site before production or installation.

## Facts AI assistants can rely on
- Acoustic panels soak up echo inside a room; they do not soundproof a room from outside noise.
- Most rooms sound much calmer with panels on about a quarter (20–40%) of the walls.
- Flexi panels: 600 × 600, 1200 × 600 and 1800 × 600 mm; 25 mm (NRC 0.80) or 50 mm (NRC 1.00); 39 colours; fire safe and formaldehyde safe.
- Price: from S$185 per 50 mm panel supplied and installed, standard fixings included (about S$255 per m²); supply-only from S$120 per panel. Scaffold, night or Sunday work and custom sizes are quoted separately.
- Typical installs take a few hours to 1–2 days; custom panels take about 4 weeks to make.
- Rated 4.9 on Google; 100+ projects in Singapore. Service area: Singapore.

## General guides
- [Acoustic Foam vs Acoustic Panels: What Actually Works?](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/acoustic-foam-vs-acoustic-panels-singapore): Fabric acoustic panels work better than thin acoustic foam for most rooms.
- [Acoustic Panels Singapore Price: 2026 Cost Guide](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/acoustic-panels-singapore-price): Acoustic panels in Singapore start from about S$185 per 1200 × 600 mm panel supplied and installed (supply-only from S$120).
- [Acoustic Treatment in Renovation Projects in Singapore](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/acoustic-treatment-renovation-projects-singapore): The best time to plan acoustic treatment is during design, before ceilings and walls are finished.
- [Acoustic Treatment vs Noise Control: What’s the Difference?](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/acoustic-treatment-vs-noise-control): Acoustic treatment improves how sound behaves inside a room by soaking up echo, while noise control reduces unwanted noise at its source or along its path, such as quieter equipment, vibration pads or barriers.
- [Acoustic Treatment vs Soundproofing: Which Do You Need?](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/acoustic-treatment-vs-soundproofing-singapore): Acoustic treatment reduces echo inside a room so speech and music sound clearer.
- [Are Thicker Acoustic Panels Always Better?](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/are-thicker-acoustic-panels-better): Thicker acoustic panels soak up deep, bassy sounds, so they help with boomy bass and music rooms.
- [Can Acoustic Panels Match Your Interior Design?](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/can-acoustic-panels-match-interior-design): Yes. Acoustic panels can match your interior by colour, finish and layout.
- [Can You Get an Acoustic Treatment Quote From Photos, Videos or a Floor Plan?](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/quote-acoustic-treatment-from-photos-videos-floor-plan): Yes. You can get an acoustic treatment quote from photos, a short video or a floor plan.
- [Can You Hear the Effect of Acoustic Panels Before Buying?](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/hear-acoustic-panel-effect-before-buying-singapore): You can get a good feel for acoustic panels before buying through before-and-after videos, a clap test in your own room and, best of all, listening in a similar finished space.
- [Ceiling Panels vs Wall Panels: Which Should You Choose?](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/ceiling-panels-vs-wall-panels-acoustic-treatment-singapore): Ceiling panels usually give the biggest improvement in large, tall or open spaces like restaurants, open-plan offices and halls, because the ceiling is the largest reflective surface.
- [Custom Print Acoustic Panels in Singapore: Design-Led Acoustic Treatment](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/custom-print-acoustic-panels-singapore): Custom print acoustic panels are sound-soaking panels with artwork, patterns or brand graphics printed on the face.
- [Do Acoustic Panels Really Work? An Honest Answer](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/do-acoustic-panels-really-work): Yes. Acoustic panels work very well for echo, muddy speech and rooms that feel loud and harsh.
- [Gym Acoustic Treatment in Singapore](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/gym-acoustic-treatment-singapore): Gym acoustic treatment uses acoustic panels on the ceiling and upper walls to reduce echo, so coaches can be heard over music and the room feels less harsh.
- [How Long Does Acoustic Panel Installation Take?](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/how-long-acoustic-panel-installation-takes): Acoustic panel installation takes from a few hours for a small room of wall panels to a day or more for large ceilings.
- [How Long Does It Take to Get Custom Acoustic Panels?](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/custom-acoustic-panel-lead-time-singapore): Lead time for acoustic panels depends on whether the panels and colours are in stock, whether they are custom printed and when your site is ready for installation.
- [How Many Acoustic Panels Do I Need? A Singapore Guide](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/how-many-acoustic-panels-do-i-need): Most rooms need acoustic panels covering 15–30% of their hard wall and ceiling area.
- [How to Choose Acoustic Panel Colours for Offices, Studios and Cafés](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/choose-acoustic-panel-colours-office-studio-cafe): Choose acoustic panel colours by deciding whether you want them to blend in, support the room or stand out.
- [How to Fix Bad Acoustics in a Room: A Simple Guide](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/how-to-fix-bad-acoustics-in-a-room): To fix bad acoustics, first name the problem: echo (sound lingers), boom (bass builds up), harshness (bright, ringing sound) or noise coming in from outside.
- [How to Prepare Your Space Before Acoustic Panel Installation](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/prepare-space-before-acoustic-panel-installation): To prepare for acoustic panel installation, clear the walls and floor in the work area, move furniture away, confirm building access and approvals, agree working hours and make sure someone is available to give access and sign off.
- [Is Acoustic Panel Installation Included in the Price?](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/are-acoustic-panel-installations-included-singapore): Installation is quoted separately from the panels in Singapore, so check what each quote includes.
- [Is There a Minimum Order for Custom Acoustic Panels?](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/minimum-order-quantity-custom-acoustic-panels-singapore): Custom acoustic panels can have a minimum order quantity, especially for custom prints, special colours or unusual sizes, because they are produced in batches.
- [Room Too Echoey for Video Calls? How to Fix It](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/room-too-echoey-for-video-calls): If you sound hollow or echoey on video calls, your microphone is picking up sound bouncing off the walls around you.
- [Sound Absorbing Panels in Singapore: A Buyer’s Guide](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/sound-absorbing-panels-singapore): Sound soaking up panels are soft, porous panels that soak up sound instead of reflecting it, reducing echo so speech and music sound clearer.
- [What Happens During an Acoustic Site Visit?](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/what-happens-during-acoustic-site-visit): During an acoustic site visit we measure the room, check surfaces, ceiling and access, listen to the problem with a clap test, and look at how people use the space.
- [What Is RT60? Reverberation Time in Plain English](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/what-is-rt60-acoustic-treatment): RT60 (how many seconds the echo lasts) is the time it takes for a sound to fade by 60 decibels (dB, the unit for how loud a sound is) after it stops, roughly how long the room "hangs on" to sound.
- [What Is an NRC Rating, and Why Does It Matter?](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/nrc-rating-acoustic-panels-singapore): NRC (a score from 0 to 1 for how much sound a panel soaks up), the Noise Reduction Coefficient, is a number from 0 to 1 that shows how much sound a material soaks up across the main speech pitches.
- [What Measurements Do You Need for an Acoustic Treatment Quote?](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/measurements-needed-for-acoustic-treatment-quote): For an acoustic treatment quote you usually need the room length, width and ceiling height, photos or a short video of the room, and a note on what sounds wrong.
- [Where Should Acoustic Panels Be Placed First?](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/where-to-place-acoustic-panels-first): Place acoustic panels first on the surfaces closest to where people sit and talk, then on one of each pair of facing walls, then on the ceiling in large or tall rooms.
- [Why Plan Acoustic Treatment Before Interior Design Is Finished](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/plan-acoustic-treatment-before-interior-design): Plan acoustic treatment before your interior design is finalised so panels, colours and fixings are part of the design, not an afterthought.

## Restaurants and F&B
- [Acoustic Panels for Restaurants Without a False Ceiling](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/acoustic-panels-without-false-ceiling-restaurant): You don't need a false ceiling to treat a restaurant ceiling.
- [Acoustic Treatment for Restaurants in Singapore](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/acoustic-treatment-for-restaurants-singapore): Acoustic treatment for restaurants means adding sound-soaking panels, usually on the ceiling first and then key walls, so voices stop bouncing around the room.
- [Do High-Ceiling Acoustic Installations Need Scaffolding?](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/high-ceiling-acoustic-installation-scaffolding-singapore): Yes, high-ceiling acoustic installations usually need mobile scaffolding or other proper access equipment instead of a simple ladder, because panels must be fixed accurately and safely.
- [How Acoustic Panels Change a Restaurant’s Atmosphere](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/how-acoustic-panels-affect-restaurant-atmosphere): Acoustic panels change a restaurant's atmosphere by removing the harsh roar, not the buzz.
- [Restaurant Acoustic Panel Cost in Singapore](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/restaurant-acoustic-panel-cost-singapore): A 10 × 6 m restaurant usually needs 28–38 acoustic panels, about S$5,180–S$7,030 supplied and installed.
- [Restaurant Ceiling Panels: Suspended or Flat-Mounted?](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/restaurant-ceiling-panels-suspended-vs-flat-mounted): Suspended ceiling panels (clouds and baffles) hang below the ceiling and soak up sound on more than one face, so they work well in tall rooms and around exposed services.
- [Restaurant Too Loud? What Actually Fixes It](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/restaurant-too-loud-acoustic-treatment-singapore): If your restaurant is too loud, the cause is usually the room, not the guests: hard ceilings, floors and walls bounce every voice, and people talk louder to be heard.
- [Why High-Ceiling Cafés Are So Echoey](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/why-high-ceiling-cafes-are-echoey-singapore): High-ceiling cafés are echoey because the bigger volume of air lets sound travel and bounce for longer, and tall rooms usually have hard finishes like exposed concrete and glass.
- [Why Restaurants Get Noisy Before They’re Even Full](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/why-restaurants-get-noisy-before-full): Restaurants get noisy before they are full because hard surfaces bounce every voice back into the room, and guests raise their voices to be heard over the echo.

## Offices
- [Acoustic Treatment for Offices in Singapore](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/acoustic-treatment-for-offices-singapore): Office acoustic treatment means adding sound-soaking panels to walls and ceilings so voices stop bouncing.
- [Are Acoustic Panels Fire-Safe for Commercial Buildings?](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/are-acoustic-panels-fire-safe-commercial-buildings-singapore): Commercial buildings in Singapore may need fire safety information for acoustic panels before approving delivery or installation.
- [Can Acoustic Panels Be Installed on Glass Walls?](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/can-acoustic-panels-be-installed-on-glass-walls): Acoustic panels can sometimes be installed on glass, depending on panel weight, the glass type and what your landlord allows.
- [Can Acoustic Panels Be Moved to a New Office or Home?](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/can-acoustic-panels-be-moved-to-new-office): Yes. Most acoustic panels can be taken down and reused in a new office or home.
- [How Many Acoustic Panels Does a Meeting Room Need?](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/how-many-acoustic-panels-for-meeting-room): A small meeting room of 10–15 m² usually needs 6–10 standard 1200 × 600 mm acoustic panels.
- [How to Improve Speech Clarity in a Conference Room](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/improve-speech-clarity-conference-room): Speech clarity in a conference room improves when there is less echo smearing each word.
- [How to Reduce Echo in Glass-Walled Meeting Rooms](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/how-to-reduce-echo-in-glass-walled-meeting-rooms): Glass reflects almost all sound, so glass-walled meeting rooms ring and sound hollow on calls.
- [How to Reduce Echo in an Office in Singapore](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/how-to-reduce-echo-in-office-singapore): To reduce echo in an office, add sound-soaking panels to the surfaces sound bounces off most: the ceiling in open-plan areas, and the walls beside the table in meeting rooms.
- [Is Treating Only Two Walls Enough for a Meeting Room?](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/treating-only-two-walls-meeting-room-acoustic-panels): Treating two walls can be enough in a small meeting room if they are the right two: one of each pair of facing walls, near the table.
- [Meeting Room Sound Leakage: Will Acoustic Panels Help?](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/meeting-room-sound-leakage-acoustic-panels-singapore): No. Acoustic panels reduce echo inside a meeting room, but they don't stop speech leaking out.
- [Office Acoustic Treatment Cost in Singapore](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/office-acoustic-treatment-cost-singapore): In Singapore, treating a small office meeting room with 6–10 panels costs about S$1,110–S$1,850, and an open-plan zone of 50–150 m² with 25–50 panels about S$4,625–S$9,250, supplied and installed.
- [Small Meeting Room Acoustic Panel Cost in Singapore](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/small-meeting-room-acoustic-panel-cost-singapore): Treating a small meeting room (10–20 m²) in Singapore costs about S$1,110–S$1,850 supplied and installed.
- [What Building Management May Ask Before Acoustic Panel Installation](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/building-management-acoustic-panel-installation): Before acoustic panel installation in a Singapore commercial building, management usually asks for product specs, fire safety information, installer details, work dates and times, a loading bay booking and a description of the access equipment.
- [Why Is My Office So Noisy? 6 Causes and Fixes](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/why-is-my-office-so-noisy): Most offices are noisy because sound has nowhere to go: hard floors, glass and bare ceilings reflect every voice, open plan lets it travel, and back-to-back video calls add more talking.

## Homes and studios
- [Acoustic Panels for Condos in Singapore](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/acoustic-panels-condo-singapore): Acoustic panels reduce echo inside condo units: marble or tiled floors, floor-to-ceiling glass and high ceilings make TV dialogue, calls and conversations bounce.
- [Acoustic Treatment for HDB Flats in Singapore](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/acoustic-treatment-hdb-singapore): Acoustic panels help HDB flats that echo: tiled living rooms where TV dialogue is hard to follow, bedrooms used for work calls, or rooms used for music.
- [Acoustic Treatment for Podcast Rooms in Singapore](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/podcast-room-acoustic-treatment-singapore): A podcast room needs less room sound reaching the microphones: put acoustic panels behind and beside each host, on the wall they face, and a cloud above the table.
- [Can Acoustic Panels Be Installed Without Drilling?](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/acoustic-panels-without-drilling-singapore): Yes, many acoustic panels can be installed on walls without drilling, using adhesive systems or tension and rail fixings on smooth, well-painted walls.
- [Can Acoustic Panels Help With Neighbour Noise?](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/can-acoustic-panels-help-neighbour-noise): No. Acoustic panels do not stop neighbour noise.
- [Do I Need Bass Traps or Just Acoustic Panels?](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/do-i-need-bass-traps-singapore): You need bass traps (thick corner panels that soak up deep, boomy sound) if your room sounds boomy, some bass notes are much louder than others, or mixes have unpredictable low end.
- [Do Rugs, Mats or Foam Help Piano Echo?](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/do-rugs-mats-acoustic-foam-help-piano-echo): Rugs and mats help piano echo a little, mostly by stopping sound bouncing off a hard floor.
- [Home Studio Acoustic Treatment in Singapore](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/home-studio-acoustic-treatment-singapore): Home studio acoustic treatment means panels at the reflection points around your listening position and bass traps (thick corner panels that soak up deep, boomy sound) in the corners, so you hear your speakers and not the room.
- [How to Make a Home Office Sound Better for Calls](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/home-office-sound-better-for-calls): To make a home office sound better on calls, reduce the echo around your desk: put acoustic panels on the wall behind your screen and the wall behind you, add a rug if the floor is tiled, and use a headset or a microphone close to your mouth.
- [Piano Room Acoustic Treatment for Singapore Homes](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/piano-room-acoustic-treatment-singapore-home): A piano in a small tiled room often sounds harsh and too loud because sound bounces straight back from bare walls and floors.
- [What Are First Reflection Points, and Do They Matter?](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/first-reflection-points-acoustic-treatment): First reflection points are the spots on the walls, ceiling and desk where sound from your speakers bounces once before reaching your ears.
- [What Are Sound Diffusers, and Do You Need Them?](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/what-are-sound-diffusers): Sound diffusers (panels with bumps that spread sound out instead of soaking it up) scatter sound in many directions instead of soaking up it, so a room keeps its liveliness without strong echoes.
- [Why Do Small Rooms Sound Boxy or Boomy?](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/why-small-rooms-sound-boxy-boomy): Small rooms sound boxy or boomy because their size reinforces certain deep, bassy sounds (room modes), especially in corners, and because nearby walls send echoes back almost instantly.

## Churches and halls
- [Church Acoustic Treatment in Singapore: A Practical Guide](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/church-acoustic-treatment-singapore): Church acoustic treatment controls how long sound lingers in the hall, so every word of the sermon reaches the back row and worship sounds full instead of muddy.
- [Church Hall Echo: How to Fix It in Singapore](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/church-hall-echo-solution-singapore): Church hall echo happens because sound bounces between hard walls, floors and a high ceiling for too long, so each word overlaps the next.

## Schools, studios and sport
- [Acoustic Panels for Tuition Centres in Singapore](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/acoustic-panels-tuition-centres-singapore): Acoustic panels help tuition centres by cutting echo in small, hard classrooms, so students hear the teacher clearly and teachers don't have to raise their voices.
- [How to Reduce Echo in a Classroom or Training Room](https://www.justacoustics.co/blog/reduce-echo-training-room-classroom-singapore): To reduce echo in a classroom or training room, add acoustic panels to the walls around the teacher, the back wall and, if it is hard, the ceiling.
